cards.title: Introduction to Control Flow
cards.content:
Control flow is the order in which individual statements, instructions, or function calls are executed or evaluated in a Python program.

By default, code runs sequentially from top to bottom. Control flow statements allow us to alter this path using conditional checks and loops.

cards.title: Conditional Statements: if, elif, else
cards.content:
Conditional statements allow your program to make decisions based on boolean expressions.

age = 18
if age >= 18:
    print("You are an adult.")
elif age > 13:
    print("You are a teenager.")
else:
    print("You are a child.")

content.question: What will be the output of: x = 10; if x > 5: print('A') elif x > 8: print('B') else: print('C')

cards.title: Iteration with While Loops
cards.content:
A while loop repeatedly executes a block of code as long as a given condition evaluates to True.

count = 0
while count < 3:
    print(count)
    count += 1

cards.title: Iteration with For Loops
cards.content:
A for loop in Python is used for iterating over a sequence (such as a list, tuple, dictionary, set, or string).

fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]
for fruit in fruits:
    print(fruit)

content.text: To iterate over a sequence of numbers in Python, such as from 0 to 4, we commonly use the ______ function inside a for loop.

cards.title: Break, Continue, and Pass
cards.content:
We can alter the behavior of loops using special statements:

  • break: Exits the loop immediately.
  • continue: Skips the current iteration and moves to the next.
  • pass: A null operation; it acts as a placeholder.
for i in range(5):
    if i == 2:
        continue
    if i == 4:
        break
    print(i)

items: If 'if' is False, evaluate the first 'elif' condition
If all previous conditions are False, execute the 'else' block
Exit the conditional block and continue program execution

cards.title: Summary & Best Practices
cards.content:
You have learned how to direct program execution using conditionals and loops in Python.

  • Always ensure loop conditions will eventually become false to prevent infinite loops.
  • Use for loops when iterating over known sequences and while loops for conditional repetitions.
  • Keep your indentation consistent, as Python relies on whitespace for block scoping.
